newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia put $122 mln in Mars probe, others $180 mln.
newsitem.headline: Russia put $122 mln in Mars probe, others $180 mln.

text.p: Russia invested $122 million in its ill-fated Mars probe and other countries put some $180 million into the scientific equipment it was carrying, Russian officials said on Monday.

Of the total $300 million lost, the probe, which fell to Earth on Sunday within hours of liftoff, had cost $86 million and about $36 million had been spent on preparing the mission, said Yuri Milov, deputy director of the Russian Space Agency.
Some 20 other countries, including the U.S., had spent around $180 million putting equipment on board the spacecraft to study conditions on the red planet, he told a news conference.
Milov said the Russian investment had not been insured because Russian law dictates that insurance must be paid for out of the agency's profits, and it did not have any.

The scientists did not cite financial problems in their explanation of the mission's failure, saying that they were still studying the possible causes, but when asked about funding, they said there were big problems, with some workers in the sector not paid for months.
"Our finances are very difficult," said Milov.

He did not think the other countries would try to make any claims against Russia. "The equipment was carried for free. It's the foreign specialists' own cost and I don't expect any claims, although of course it's painful for us that they've spent it for nothing," he said.
"We've put seven years work into this," said Nikolai Ivanov, head of the main operational group controlling the mission. "I cannot begin to describe how it feels."
